The demand profile for the month showed a clear bifurcation: pre-monsoon days (01–19 June) saw afternoon peaks averaging 2,150 kW, while post-monsoon-onset days (20–30 June) averaged 1,740 kW. The minimum daily demand of 980 kW was recorded on 22 June (Sunday), when campus occupancy was at its lowest.

**8. Grid Import & Power Quality**

Grid import for June was **322,530 kWh**, which is the net of total consumption minus solar generation (90,120 kWh) and BESS discharge (18,450 kWh), with BESS charging (19,120 kWh) added back. This aligns with the monthly meter readings. Grid import was 4.1% lower than May's figure of 336,280 kWh.

Power quality events: Two voltage sags were recorded on 12 June (08:12, depth 12%, duration 1.2 seconds) and 27 June (19:48, depth 8%, duration 0.8 seconds). Both events originated from the utility side and did not trip any critical load. The Data Centre UPS handled both events without transfer to battery, and no equipment damage was reported. The Electrical Maintenance team has logged these events for the quarterly utility review.

Total campus consumption for June 2025 was **432,100 kWh**, a decrease of 2.8% compared to May 2025 (444,550 kWh). Solar generation contributed **90,120 kWh**, meeting 20.9% of total demand. Grid import was **322,530 kWh**, down 4.1% from May. Peak demand of 2,340 kW was recorded on 04 June; the month saw a clear demand reduction following monsoon onset on 20 June.

Total campus consumption for June 2025 was 1,842,560 kWh, a decrease of 3.2% compared to May 2025 (1,903,410 kWh). The reduction is primarily attributed to the onset of the monsoon season, which moderated cooling loads during the latter half of the month. Solar generation for the month was 118,340 kWh, representing 6.4% of total campus consumption. This is a slight decline from May (124,890 kWh) due to overcast conditions.

Battery storage activity was moderate, with the system completing 18 full charge-discharge cycles. The storage system provided 42,150 kWh of energy during peak evening hours, contributing to demand management. The peak demand for the month was recorded on 11 June at 14:35 hours.

---

**2. CAMPUS CONSUMPTION OVERVIEW**

The following table presents consumption data by building for June 2025, with comparisons to May 2025.

*Note: Consumption figures are aggregated by meter and include all connected loads. Rounding may cause minor discrepancies in totals.*

---

**3. SOLAR GENERATION**

Solar PV generation for June 2025 totalled 118,340 kWh. The daily average generation was 3,945 kWh, compared to 4,029 kWh in May 2025. The reduction is consistent with the transition to monsoon conditions, which began around 15 June.

The Roof Solar Array, installed on Tower B, remains the primary generation asset on campus. The array's peak capacity is 500 kW. The system operated without any major outages during the month. A minor inverter alarm was logged on 22 June, which was cleared remotely the same day.

**4. BATTERY STORAGE SYSTEM**

The battery storage system completed 18 charge-discharge cycles during June 2025. Total energy discharged during peak hours was 42,150 kWh. The system's round-trip efficiency averaged 88.2%, slightly lower than the May average of 89.1%. This is attributed to higher ambient temperatures during the first half of the month.

The storage system was primarily used for peak shaving between 17:00 and 21:30 hours. On 11 June, the system discharged at its maximum rate for 2.5 hours to support the campus during a grid voltage fluctuation. No damage or degradation was noted.

The maximum demand for June 2025 was recorded on 11 June at 14:35 hours. The exact demand value is being verified by the utility and will be reported in the next monthly statement. Preliminary estimates place the demand at approximately 4,150 kVA.

Demand management measures, including the use of battery storage during evening peaks, contributed to a 2.8% reduction in average peak demand compared to May 2025.

---

**6. COMPARISON WITH PREVIOUS MONTHS**

Consumption in June 2025 was the lowest since February 2025 (1,798,650 kWh). The monsoon onset is expected to further reduce cooling loads in July.

**7. NOTES AND OBSERVATIONS**

- The Data Centre (BLD-F) showed the smallest reduction in consumption (-0.98%), consistent with its continuous load profile.
- Solar generation on 04 June was the highest for the month at 4,680 kWh, while the lowest was on 27 June at 2,940 kWh.

1. Investigate the slight reduction in battery round-trip efficiency during high-temperature periods.
2. Monitor the Roof Solar Array performance during the monsoon months to identify any moisture-related issues.
3. Review the evening peak demand profile to optimise the battery discharge schedule for July.

**4. Battery Storage & Demand Management**

The battery energy storage system (BESS) supported peak demand management throughout June, particularly during the evening peak window (18:00–21:00). Total discharge for the month was **18,450 kWh**, while total charge was **19,120 kWh**, reflecting a round-trip efficiency of 96.5%. The system completed 28 full charge-discharge cycles, with an average depth of discharge of 82%.

**5. Battery Storage & Demand Management (Continued)**

The BESS also contributed to ancillary services on two days when grid voltage fluctuations were observed. On 12 June and 27 June, the system was dispatched in a frequency-regulation mode for 45 minutes and 30 minutes respectively, discharging a combined 340 kWh during these intervals. These events were logged but did not require manual intervention.

Battery degradation metrics for June: average cell temperature remained within the 28–34°C band, and the thermal management system consumed 1,120 kWh, slightly higher than May's 1,080 kWh due to the warmer first fortnight.

**6. Campus Consumption Summary**

Total campus consumption for June 2025 was **412,650 kWh**. This represents a 3.2% decrease compared to May 2025 (426,180 kWh) and a 1.8% decrease compared to June 2024 (420,210 kWh). The reduction is primarily attributable to the monsoon-related drop in HVAC load and the partial occupancy during the examination week (16–20 June), when academic buildings operated at reduced capacity.

| Building / Meter Group | June 2025 (kWh) | May 2025 (kWh) | Change (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Academic Blocks A & B | 118,240 | 124,510 | -5.0 |
| Central Library | 21,340 | 22,180 | -3.8 |
| Administrative Block | 28,560 | 29,740 | -4.0 |
| Hostels (all) | 96,870 | 95,420 | +1.5 |
| Cafeteria & Student Centre | 14,230 | 14,860 | -4.2 |
| Sports Complex | 18,920 | 19,340 | -2.2 |
| Guest House | 6,410 | 6,220 | +3.1 |
| Central Plant & Utilities (excluding HVAC) | 42,380 | 44,120 | -3.9 |
| Street Lighting & Common Areas | 17,940 | 18,320 | -2.1 |
| Data Centre & IT Services | 47,760 | 51,470 | -7.2 |
| **Total** | **412,650** | **426,180** | **-3.2** |

The Data Centre & IT Services meter group recorded the largest percentage reduction, driven by the migration of two non-critical virtual servers to a cloud provider and the decommissioning of one legacy storage array. This was a planned efficiency measure approved in the May Energy Review Committee meeting.

Hostel consumption increased by 1.5%, attributed to higher fan and cooler usage during the humid pre-monsoon days in the first fortnight. The Guest House uptick is linked to a three-day conference (18–20 June) that hosted external delegates.

**7. Demand Profile & Peak Load**

The maximum demand recorded in June was **2,340 kW** on 04 June at 15:40, coinciding with the peak ambient temperature day. The evening peak window (18:00–21:00) saw an average demand of 1,890 kW, which was successfully managed through BESS discharge and scheduled load shifting of the central plant's chilled water pumps.

The demand profile for the month showed a clear bifurcation: pre-monsoon days (01–19 June) saw afternoon peaks averaging 2,150 kW, while post-monsoon-onset days (20–30 June) averaged 1,740 kW. The minimum daily demand of 980 kW was recorded on 22 June (Sunday), when campus occupancy was at its lowest.

**8. Grid Import & Power Quality**

Grid import for June was **322,530 kWh**, which is the net of total consumption minus solar generation (90,120 kWh) and BESS discharge (18,450 kWh), with BESS charging (19,120 kWh) added back. This aligns with the monthly meter readings. Grid import was 4.1% lower than May's figure of 336,280 kWh.

Power quality events: Two voltage sags were recorded on 12 June (08:12, depth 12%, duration 1.2 seconds) and 27 June (19:48, depth 8%, duration 0.8 seconds). Both events originated from the utility side and did not trip any critical load. The Data Centre UPS handled both events without transfer to battery, and no equipment damage was reported. The Electrical Maintenance team has logged these events for the quarterly utility review.

**Monthly Energy Report – Campus Overview**
**Reporting Period: 01 June 2025 – 30 June 2025**
**Issue Date: 07 July 2025**
**Prepared by: Energy Analytics Group**

---

**1. Executive Summary**

Total campus consumption for June 2025 was **432,100 kWh**, a decrease of 2.8% compared to May 2025 (444,550 kWh). Solar generation contributed **90,120 kWh**, meeting 20.9% of total demand. The Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) completed 142 full charge/discharge cycles, with a net discharge of **18,450 kWh** and charging draw of **19,120 kWh**, resulting in a round-trip efficiency of 96.5%. Grid import was **322,530 kWh**, down 4.1% from May. Peak demand of 2,340 kW was recorded on 04 June; the month saw a clear demand reduction following monsoon onset on 20 June.

---

**2. Consumption by Meter Group**

Street lighting shows the largest percentage reduction, attributed to the completion of the LED retrofit project in the second week of June and shorter night durations post-monsoon onset. The Guest House increase is linked to the three-day conference (18–20 June) hosting external delegates. Hostel consumption rose marginally due to humid pre-monsoon conditions in the first fortnight.

---

**3. Solar Generation**

Total solar generation for June was **90,120 kWh**, a 3.1% increase over May's 87,410 kWh. Generation was higher in the first half of the month, with clear skies and high insolation. Post-monsoon-onset days (20–30 June) saw average daily generation drop by 22% due to cloud cover.

No major inverter faults were reported. Two string-level underperformance issues (Array A2 and Array G4) were identified during routine I-V curve testing on 16 June; both were traced to soiling and were resolved by cleaning on 18 June. Generation data is recorded at 15-minute intervals and aggregated daily.

---

**4. Battery Energy Storage System (BESS)**

The BESS (2 MW / 4 MWh, Li-ion) operated throughout June. Total charging draw was **19,120 kWh**; total discharge was **18,450 kWh**. The system completed 142 cycles, with a round-trip efficiency of 96.5%. BESS discharge was primarily scheduled during the evening peak window (18:00–21:00) to manage demand, with additional discharge events on 04, 12, and 27 June corresponding to power quality events.

|---|---|

| Discharge (kWh) | 18,450 |

| Round-trip efficiency (%) | 96.5 |
| Peak discharge rate (kW) | 1,850 (04 June, 17:55) |

The BESS was unavailable for 6.2 hours on 21 June for scheduled preventive maintenance (coolant top-up and contactor inspection). No performance degradation was observed during the month.

---

**5. Grid Import & Power Quality**

Grid import for June was **322,530 kWh**, which is the net of total consumption minus solar generation (90,120 kWh) and BESS discharge (18,450 kWh), with BESS charging (19,120 kWh) added back. This aligns with the monthly meter readings. Grid import was 4.1% lower than May's figure of 336,280 kWh.
